annotations.text:
Today

What ships now, drawn to touch.lua's geometry. All five complaints on one board: the charge cells are gold squares, the gun's whole loadout is squeezed into the pad until the fan stops reading, the multifire arrow is nine pixels, the stick is a bare wireframe ring, and nothing anywhere says a double tap reverses.

A · Instrument

The pads become cockpit gauges: radial glow, a hairline ring, a bright rim arc. The volley draws at full size because the add-on ladder moved out to rung ticks on the rim. Multifire is a tab on the gun's rim wearing the fan at a size that reads; a tap toggles it and the upward pull still works. Charges are hexagonal cells counting in dashes. The stick is a rose with rim ticks, a nose chevron, and a stance tab at its foot: tap the tab or double tap the half to flip, and reversed the whole instrument turns engine orange.

Cost: the most ink of the three, and the rim tab wants vertical room in the corner the radar already borders.

B · Cluster

No boxes anywhere: one big key for the gun, the trigger a thumb lives on, and one orbit of satellites at charge size for everything it visits: bomb, repel, burst, an even fifty degrees apart. The marks alone name the keys. A charge key's count ring is its whole boundary: one rim segment per charge, dimming as they spend, and a key spent out stays where it is, dimmed whole, until the rack fills again; the bomb keeps its ring whole, which is what says trigger rather than charge. There is no multifire toggle on a phone: the gun's mark simply draws the volley the trigger will throw, and declining the fan stays a keyboard matter. The stick rests as a quiet ring with the gesture etched around its foot, always naming what the next double tap does: TAP ×2 · REVERSE at rest, TAP ×2 · FORWARD while reversed. Held, it grows a course needle, and reversed the needle swings to the far side of the thumb.

The states board below shows a charge key at three, two and one in hand, and spent.

Cost: the bomb at satellite size is a smaller target for a held trigger, and a phone pilot cannot decline the fan mid-fight.

C · Glass

No chrome at all: each control is its glowing mark over a barely-there footprint, so the fight stays the whole picture. The gun is its volley: multifire on is three rounds, declined is one lit and two dim, and the state is the drawing. Counts are bare pips. The stick is a reticle of four arcs with a ghost hint that fades once the gesture has been used.

Cost: the quietest resting state is also the least discoverable one, and a footprint you cannot see is an edge you find by missing.

Held constant on every board: one duel, Vesper 412 against Mantis 7, the shipped chrome (MENU, score band, radar), palette.lua's hues exactly (rung 2 gun yellow, rung 3 bomb orange, charge gold, thrust orange for the reversed stance), and marks.lua's drawings of a round, a bomb, a repel and a burst.

Two proposals hold whatever the direction: multifire gets a drawn state of its own instead of a compressed loadout mark, and reverse gets a visible control a thumb can also tap, so the double tap becomes the shortcut rather than the secret.

The lower row is the reversed stance with the stick engaged: the course points away from the thumb, the nose stays on the fight, and the ship burns its retros out of the bow.
